{{Short description|Serbian mathematician}}
{{About|the mathematician|the actress|Natasha Pavlovich}}'''Nataša Pavlović''' is a Serbian mathematician who works as a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Texas at Austin]].
Her research concerns [[fluid dynamics]] and nonlinear [[dispersive partial differential equation]]s.<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=https://www.ma.utexas.edu/users/natasa/cv2017Sep29w.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae: Nataša Pavlović|accessdate=2018-03-28}}.</ref>
She is known for her work with [[Nets Katz]] pioneering an approach to constructing singularities in equations resembling the [[Navier–Stokes equations]], by transferring a finite amount of energy through an infinitely decreasing sequence of time and length scales.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/20140224-a-fluid-new-path-in-grand-math-challenge/|title=A Fluid New Path in Grand Math Challenge|magazine=Quanta|date=February 24, 2014|first=Erica|last=Klarreich}}.</ref>

Pavlović earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from the [[University of Belgrade]] in 1996, and completed her doctorate from the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]] in 2002 under the joint supervision of [[Susan Friedlander]] and Nets Katz.<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=64719}}</ref> After temporary positions at the [[Clay Mathematics Institute]], [[Princeton University]], [[Institute for Advanced Study]], and [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]], she joined the Princeton faculty in 2005, and moved to the University of Texas in 2007.<ref name="cv"/>

She was a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Research Fellow]] from 2008 to 2012.
In 2015 she was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2016 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=2015-11-19}}.</ref> From 2013-2015, Pavlović served as a Council Member at Large for the American Mathematical Society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-27 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref> She was elected a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web | title = Electing New Members: Recognizing America’s 250th Anniversary | url = https://www.amacad.org/news/new-member-announcement-2026 | website = American Academy of Arts and Sciences}}</ref>
